title: SLO calibration & eval matrix for batching and prefix-caching tradeoffs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Run a controlled evaluation to map latency vs. quality tradeoffs across a sweep of batching and prefix (KV) cache configurations, produce SLO-calibrated guardrails, and generate rollout guidance. This ticket ties eval outputs to alert thresholds and rollout policies for per-route configs. Goal is to avoid silent quality regressions while recovering cost/latency improvements from batching and cache aggressiveness.
acceptance_criteria: Full experiment matrix executed on representative workload (prod-sampled and synthetic long-context)
Lat+quality Pareto curves and SLO calibration documented in a single confluence page
Suggested guardrail thresholds for p50/p95 latency and quality regression deltas linked to automated alerts
Runbook for rollback and canary thresholds for config rollouts created
Benchmarks and artifacts (plots, raw eval outputs, PRs) uploaded to runtime-evals folder
evaluation_plan: Select three model variants (base fp16, int8 quant, int8+kv-optimized) and two sequence-length profiles (short, long)
Select traffic slices: 1) production-sampled 100k requests across routes, 2) instruction-following eval set (~5k), 3) long-context creative set (~2k)
Define config axes: microbatch size (1/4/8), batch timeout (5/10/25 ms), kv cache ttl/eviction aggressiveness (conservative/moderate/aggressive)
Run each config combination through the eval harness capturing latency histograms, token throughput, and quality metrics (semantic similarity, instruction compliance, token-level logprob deltas)
Run each experiment with 3 replicates across different cluster nodes to capture hardware noise
Aggregate outputs and compute regression deltas vs baseline (current default config)
Produce per-route recommendations and SLO guardrails, then synthesize a rollout plan
experiment_matrix: Variants: [microbatch=1,4,8] x [batch_timeout=5,10,25ms] x [kv_eviction=conservative,moderate,aggressive] => 27 configs per model/seqlen
SeqLen profiles: short (<=128 tokens typical), long (>=1024 tokens heavy-context)
Replica runs: each config x model x seqlen x 3 repeats => full matrix (~486 runs per seqlen per model)
Traffic mixes: weighted by route QPS for production-sampled slice and uniform for synthetic sets
metrics: Latency: p50, p95, p99 server-side tail latencies (ms) and token-generation latency (ms/token)
Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec under production concurrency
Quality: instruction-following accuracy (human-eval proxy), semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), and aggregate logprob delta vs baseline
Regression metrics: fraction of prompts with quality drop > 1% / 3% / 5% and mean delta
Stability: variance across replicates and host-level noise (stddev of p95)
Cost-proxy: GPU-seconds per 1k requests and estimated token-cost delta
dataset_and_prompts: prod-sampled-traces: anonymized 100k requests from Feb 2026 (balanced by route)
instruction-following-set: 5k labeled examples (internal eval suite) with expected outputs for compliance scoring
long-context-creative: 2k prompts designed to force long KV cache usage and attention patterns
edge-cases: 500 prompts focusing on hallucination-sensitive facts and SQL/code generation
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Lab-only run and PR with artifacts -> runtime-evals confluence page
Stage 2: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic on non-critical routes with aggressive telemetry for 48h
Stage 3: Expand to 25% with automated quality checks; if any route exceeds regression thresholds, rollback
Stage 4: Full rollout with monitoring thresholds converted to steady-state SLO alerts
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboards: per-route latency vs quality scatter with Pareto front overlay
Automated alert: 'quality-regression-large' triggers if >1% of prompts show quality drop >3% over a 1h window
Automated alert: 'latency-slo-breach' triggers if p95 exceeds calibrated SLO for 5m
Regression detector: daily drift job that recomputes embedding-similarity deltas against a fixed gold-set
Link alerts to rollback runbook and automatic traffic-shift to compatible model variant

2026-03-13 - Priya Natarajan (SRE): Noted that host-side GC noise may be inflating p95. Suggested pinning runs to reserved nodes for stable baselining.
2026-03-14 - Marco Lee: Adjusted plan to include reserved-node replicates and added embedding-based hallucination checks. Kicking off full matrix tomorrow.
follow_ups: If aggressive kv eviction yields unacceptable quality loss, iterate on hybrid policy: keep recent prefixes for 2x TTL when sequence length >512
Integrate selected guardrails into console rollout UI as recommended presets
Add an automated experiment to continuously monitor config drift after rollout
notes: Trade-offs observed so far: microbatching reduces per-token overhead but increases head latency for single-request flows; combining moderate batch_timeout with conservative kv eviction often yields best balanced Pareto points
Decision: prioritize route-level SLOs over global defaults; different routes will get different presets based on sensitivity to quality vs cost
Open question: whether to expose kv_eviction preset names or numeric TTL to customers in the console
